title: The disturbed galactic duo NGC 3169 and NGC 3166
caption: The interacting galaxies NGC 3169 and NGC 3166, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: NGC 3166, NGC 3169 · constellation Sextans · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two galaxies sit side by side, NGC 3169 on the left and NGC 3166 on the right. At the bottom right of the pair, a third galaxy appears, NGC 3165. The picture was taken with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager, at La Silla Observatory in Chile.

The two main galaxies are close enough that each feels the other's gravity, and both carry the scars. They are locked in a gravitational tug of war. In NGC 3169, the spiral shape has been bent out of true, warped by its neighbor's pull.

In NGC 3166 the damage shows in its dust lanes, the dark bands of dust that normally trace a galaxy's structure, which have been broken into fragments. Such interactions are common among galaxies, and over long spans of time they can reshape them completely.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (21.43 x 21.43 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 436,000 × 436,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, using blue, visual and red filters in visible light. The source does not publish the color mapping.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye can, revealing faint distortions no one could see looking through a telescope.

explore: The pair lies about 70 million light-years away in the constellation Sextans. They are classed as an interacting pair, galaxies whose mutual gravity is visibly changing them.
alt: Two galaxies side by side, a warped spiral on the left and a companion on the right, with a third galaxy at bottom right.
